title: Update dependency hugo to v0.167.0
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [hugo](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo) | uses-with | minor | `0.166.0` → `0.167.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>gohugoio/hugo (hugo)</summary>

### [`v0.167.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/releases/tag/v0.167.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/compare/v0.166.0...v0.167.0)

This release brings relative partial references, slug support for branch pages, and a handful of security hardening fixes.

**Relative partial references.** A partial name starting with `./` or `../` is now resolved relative to the directory of the calling partial. This makes it much easier to write self-contained, movable partial trees, e.g. `{{ partial "./item.html" . }}` from within `layouts/_partials/card/list.html`. Relative paths are only allowed from within partials, and paths resolving outside the partials directory is an error. See [#​15373](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15373) and the [documentation](https://gohugo.io/functions/partials/include/#relative-paths).

**Slugs for section, taxonomy and term pages.** The `slug` front matter now works for branch pages, not just regular pages, and it cascades to descendants. This is particularly useful in multilingual sites, where e.g. `content/help/_index.es.md` with `slug: ayuda` gives `/es/ayuda/`, `/es/ayuda/avanzado/` etc. See [#​14352](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/14352).

**Other notable improvements** include the new `build.cleanDestinationDir` config with `keepFiles`/`keepDirs` Glob patterns ([#​14937](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/14937), [docs](https://gohugo.io/configuration/build/#clean-destination-directory)), `hugo` now builds without a config file ([#​15393](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15393)), exact numeric comparisons in `eq`, `where`, `in` and the set functions ([#​15322](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15322), [#​15358](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15358)), and automatic summaries that no longer end inside an open list or blockquote ([#​14044](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/14044)).

#### Security

This release contains several hardening fixes. None of them are known to be exploited, but if you build sites with untrusted themes or modules, you should upgrade.

- Sass imports not found in Hugo's file systems were resolved by the Sass compiler itself, which follows symlinks and knows nothing about the project root. A theme could import a file outside the project and get its content into the published CSS. These imports are now resolved by Hugo and checked against the same `security.allowRead` roots as the Node.js tools and `js.Build`. [`41040cc`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/41040cc7) (thanks to [@​Hama1cco](https://redirect.github.com/Hama1cco))
- Likewise, imports not found in `/assets` were resolved and read by ESBuild itself. The resolved path is now checked against the allowed read paths before ESBuild loads it. [`2aa51f3`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/2aa51f34) (thanks to [@​Hama1cco](https://redirect.github.com/Hama1cco))
- A symlinked directory in a theme at the parent of a nested mount could expose files outside the module. [`2fe9bab`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/2fe9bab7)
- Explicit heading IDs (e.g. `## Foo {id="..."}`) were written unescaped into the table of contents `href`, allowing attribute breakout. [`671fbf2`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/671fbf2c)

#### Note

- The default `baseURL` is now `https://example.org/` (it was empty). Hugo has always required a valid URL to work properly, so this mostly affects new and test sites, but if you relied on the empty default for relative URLs, set `baseURL` explicitly. [`bc68654`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/bc686541) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​14625](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/14625) [#​15384](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15384)
- The root `cleanDestinationDir` config key is deprecated in favour of `build.cleanDestinationDir.enable`. The `--cleanDestinationDir` flag maps to the new key. Note that `.git` files in the publish dir are now kept by default. [`9086193`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/90861931) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​14937](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/14937)
- `eq` now compares numeric values the same way as `lt`, `le` etc., so e.g. `eq 1 1.0` is now `true`. Also, `in`, `intersect`, `union`, `uniq`, `symdiff`, `complement` and `where`'s `in`/`not in` now compare numbers exactly rather than via `float64`, and no longer require the Go types to match. [`4d628bb`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/4d628bbd) [`366377b`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/366377b6) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​15322](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15322) [#​15358](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15358)
- A user table render hook is now preferred over the embedded one. [`140d936`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/140d9362) [@​jmooring](https://redirect.github.com/jmooring) [#​15389](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/15389)
- Automatic summaries are expanded past `summaryLength` when needed so they don't end inside an open container element. This may change the summary for some pages. [`d692a24`](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/commit/d692a243) [@​bep](https://redirect.github.com/bep) [#​14044](https://redirect.github.com/gohugoio/hugo/issues/14044)

title: bug: CREATE SEQUENCE concatenates option clauses in SQL()
body:
Multiple sequence-option clauses parse, but `SQL()` joins them without spaces. The resulting keywords cannot be reparsed. This is an unparser defect independent of later validation of sequence options.

Reproduced with v0.8.1:

```sh
go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@v0.8.1 -output unparse \
  'CREATE SEQUENCE S BIT_REVERSED_POSITIVE START COUNTER WITH 1 OPTIONS (skip_range_min=10, skip_range_max=20)'
```

```text
--- SQL
CREATE SEQUENCE S BIT_REVERSED_POSITIVESTART COUNTER WITH 1 OPTIONS (skip_range_min = 10, skip_range_max = 20)
```

title: FROM-led subqueries are not recognized in several query contexts
body:
The query parser supports FROM-led queries, but the subquery lookahead recognizes SELECT only. IN, scalar, and table-subquery contexts consequently reject a supported query start.

A managed Spanner read-only probe on 2026-09-23 returned TRUE for the IN query below. Scalar and table cases are locally verified; no claim of managed execution is made for those variants.

Reproduced with v0.8.1:

```sh
go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@v0.8.1 -output unparse \
  'SELECT 1 IN (FROM UNNEST([1])) AS result'
```

```text
--- Error
syntax error: :1:14: unexpected token: FROM
  1|  SELECT 1 IN (FROM UNNEST([1])) AS result
   |               ^~~~
syntax error: :1:14: expected token: ), but: FROM
  1|  SELECT 1 IN (FROM UNNEST([1])) AS result
   |               ^~~~

--- SQL
SELECT 1 IN (FROM UNNEST([1])) AS result
```

title: test: require successful reparsing of golden SQL
body:
- Fixes #464.

Fail positive golden tests when reparsing `SQL()` returns an error, and run
round-trip checks before writing updated goldens. Keep error recovery allowed
for `!bad_` fixtures.

Validation: `make ci` and full `make update-result` with no golden changes.
Using #425 as an isolated negative control, both normal tests and `-update`
reject the invalid serialization that previously passed.

title: Golden tests ignore errors when reparsing SQL() output
body:
The golden harness discards the error from parsing `Node.SQL()`, so parser recovery may conceal an invalid serialization. In update mode, it returns before the round-trip check altogether. This is distinct from the fuzz-test proposal in #415.

This is a narrow oracle correction, not a proposal to require full AST equality or prohibit intentional SQL normalization.

At 1691dd67(the latest `origin/main`), the reparse uses `node1, _ := parse(p1)`. In an isolated harness copy, adding a positive `SELECT WITH(0)` fixture and running `-update` succeeds even though its output `SELECT WITH(, 0)` cannot parse without recovery. The corrected oracle rejects it. The WITH expression defect itself is tracked in #425.

title: bug: ChangeStreamForAll.End() extends beyond the input
body:
`CREATE CHANGE STREAM C FOR ALL` parses without error, but the root End is 33 for a 30-byte input. Slicing the source with this range panics. The ALTER form is also affected. The parser records the next token's position instead of ALL's position.

Reproduced with v0.8.1:

```go
sql := "CREATE CHANGE STREAM C FOR ALL"
n, err := memefish.ParseDDL("", sql)
fmt.Println(err, n.End(), len(sql)) // <nil> 33 30
```

title: bug: Hexadecimal and octal STRING escapes lose their Unicode values
body:
The lexer decodes hexadecimal and octal escapes as bytes even in STRING literals. Parsing and serializing a valid query can therefore replace its value with U+FFFD. Quoted identifiers use the same decoder; BYTES literals must keep their byte semantics.

The [lexical reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/lexical#escape_sequences) distinguishes Unicode characters in STRING from bytes in BYTES. A managed Spanner read-only probe on 2026-09-23 returned `ÿ` for `SELECT '\xff'`; the local result below loses that value.

Reproduced with v0.8.1:

```sh
go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@v0.8.1 -output unparse \
  'SELECT '\''\xff'\'''
```

```text
--- SQL
SELECT "�"
```

title: bug: SQL() drops required quotes from GQL graph-pattern variables
body:
- Part of #434.

Managed Spanner executes this query and returns `1`:

```sql
GRAPH FinGraph MATCH (`WALK`) RETURN 1 AS result LIMIT 1
```

However, memefish v0.8.1 removes the required quotes:

```text
$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@v0.8.1 \
    -output unparse 'GRAPH FinGraph MATCH (`WALK`) RETURN 1 AS result'
--- SQL
GRAPH FinGraph MATCH (WALK) RETURN 1 AS result
```

The output fails to reparse. Managed Spanner also rejects the unquoted node form.
The same service distinction was verified for `TRAIL`, `SIMPLE`, `ACYCLIC`,
`PATH`, and `PATHS`.

These six names are [reserved in graph-pattern identifier positions](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/d82db99a923a46571f543a13899dc791a7b6f743/googlesql/parser/googlesql.tm#L8144-L8163),
not globally reserved SQL keywords. Preserve their quoting in node, edge, and
path variable declarations without changing ordinary SQL identifiers or labels.

title: bug: SQL() drops required quotes from ordinary function names
body:
- Part of #434.

Quoted `SAFE_CAST` and `REPLACE_FIELDS` parse as ordinary function calls, but
`SQL()` removes their quotes:

```text
$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@v0.8.1 \
    -output unparse 'SELECT `SAFE_CAST`(1)'
--- SQL
SELECT SAFE_CAST(1)
```

Reparsing the output fails with `expected token: AS, but: )`.
The equivalent `REPLACE_FIELDS` call fails with `expected token: ,, but: )`.

Managed Spanner distinguishes these forms too: the quoted call reaches
`Function not found`, whereas the unquoted output is a syntax error. This is
syntax acceptance, not a claim that either ordinary function exists.

`CallExpr.SQL()` should keep the quotes needed to preserve an ordinary call,
without changing real special forms or reserving these names globally.

title: bug: SAFE_CAST and REPLACE_FIELDS cannot be used as ordinary identifiers
body:
- Part of #434.

`SAFE_CAST` and `REPLACE_FIELDS` are non-reserved names. Managed Spanner executes
`SELECT SAFE_CAST FROM (SELECT 1 AS SAFE_CAST)` and the equivalent
`REPLACE_FIELDS` query, returning `1`. Paths such as `SAFE_CAST.x` also work.

However, memefish v0.8.1 treats either name as special syntax even without `(`:

```text
$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@v0.8.1 \
    -output unparse 'SELECT SAFE_CAST'
--- Error
syntax error: :1:17: expected token: (, but: <eof>
  1|  SELECT SAFE_CAST
   |                  ^

--- SQL
SELECT SAFE_CAST
```

Only select the special-form parser when the next token is `(`; otherwise accept
the name as an identifier or path component. This matches the ambiguity resolution
described in [googlesql.tm](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/d82db99a923a46571f543a13899dc791a7b6f743/googlesql/parser/googlesql.tm#L868-L894).

```
CREATE PROPERTY GRAPH FinGraphPersonWithMetadata
```

title: Reduce state-restoration mistakes with shared parser lookahead helpers
body:
Lookahead and trial parsing require repetitive but correctness-sensitive state management. Hand-written save/restore code can omit diagnostics, miss an early return or panic path, or behave incorrectly when nested. Restoring lexer position alone does not necessarily undo a trial parse.

Centralizing this machinery would let us implement and test restoration once, reducing what each caller must get right and each reviewer must check. The goal is fewer opportunities for inconsistent state handling, not merely less boilerplate.

Related: #434 motivates reviewing disambiguation, but its individual bug fixes need not wait for this proposal.

## Proposed direction

Consider callback-based helpers sharing an audited checkpoint:

- **Lookahead:** run a callback and always restore checkpointed state.
- **Trial parsing:** retain state only when a callback explicitly accepts the interpretation; otherwise restore it.

Callbacks can perform arbitrary lexer/parser logic rather than only match fixed token sequences. Introduce helpers at demonstrated call sites; add the committing form only where retaining a tentative result is useful. Naming remains open, and existing optional `tryParse*` methods should not be assumed to guarantee rollback.

## Required behavior

- Audit the state to save, including lexer state, diagnostics, and aliasing; restore it on rollback and escaping panic without swallowing unexpected panics.
- Support nested checkpoints: inner success must remain reversible by an outer rollback.
- Keep grammar decisions with callers. A returned AST or recovery node is not necessarily a match; after identifying a construct, retain its real errors rather than trying unrelated alternatives.
- Define side-effect restrictions: captured variables and mutations to existing ASTs are not automatically rolled back.

## Validation

Test success, non-match, diagnostic appends, panic, and nested rollback. After restoration, subsequent parsing should match an untouched checkpoint. Retain focused malformed-input goldens at migrated call sites; property/fuzz tests can extend coverage of restoration invariants.

## Reference

- TypeScript uses [`lookAhead`, `tryParse` (internally uses `speculationHelper`)](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/blob/v7.0.2/src/compiler/parser.ts#L2256-L2306)

title: Handle pseudo-keywords consistently in identifier positions
body:
memefish should accept identifiers allowed by Spanner GoogleSQL, without introducing additional reserved words or quoting requirements. Non-reserved words used in syntax (pseudo-keywords) must still work as identifiers where the grammar permits them.

## Confirmed examples

`CONSTRAINT`, `FOREIGN`, `CHECK`, `PRIMARY`, and `SYNONYM` are not [reserved keywords](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/lexical#reserved_keywords). All five work as unquoted BOOL column names in `CREATE TABLE` on managed Spanner, Omni 2026.r2.1-beta, and emulator 1.5.57 (verified on 2026-09-07), but memefish rejects them at `b1e2fe7`.

Quoting these names is not a round-trip workaround: they parse, but `SQL()` removes the quotes and the output fails to reparse.

One reproduction with v0.8.1 (Go toolchain messages omitted):

```sql
$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@v0.8.1 \
    -output unparse \
    'CREATE TABLE Probe (Id INT64 NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT BOOL) PRIMARY KEY (Id)'
--- Error
syntax error: :1:55: unknown constraint
  1|  CREATE TABLE Probe (Id INT64 NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT BOOL) PRIMARY KEY (Id)
   |                                                        ^

--- SQL
CREATE TABLE Probe (Id INT64 NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT BOOL) PRIMARY KEY (Id)
```

The emulator also has [parser tests distinguishing pseudo-keyword column names from constraints](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/fc811a1a93c7e4784db7f48fe15e72fe94f39d38/backend/schema/parser/ddl_parser_test.cc#L4113-L4178), including a column named `FOREIGN` with proto type `KEY`.

## Work to track

- [ ] Fix the five CREATE TABLE cases without breaking genuine constraint/synonym syntax.
- [ ] Audit other identifier positions for the same pseudo-keyword dispatch problem and track confirmed cases here.
- [ ] Add regressions for quoted/unquoted names, correct AST interpretation, SQL round trips, and malformed clauses.

title: Join.SQL() drops the parsed HASH join method

```sql
--- SQL
SELECT * FROM A INNER JOIN B ON A.id = B.id
```

title: Accept string-valued single-part INTERVAL literals
body:
Managed Spanner (and GoogleSQL frontend) executes this query successfully:

```text
spanner> SELECT INTERVAL '1' DAY AS i;
```

```text
--- Error
syntax error: :1:25: expected token: TO, but: AS

```

title: bug: CREATE MODEL rejects arrays of structs and sized fields within structs
body:
`CREATE MODEL` supports top-level `STRUCT` after #269, but some combinations of schema types still fail to parse: `ARRAY<STRUCT<...>>` and sized `STRING`/`BYTES` fields inside a `STRUCT`.

### Documentation and upstream evidence

The official [text embeddings tutorial](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/ml-tutorial-embeddings#generate_and_store_text_embeddings) uses this output column in its `CREATE MODEL` example:

```sql
embeddings
  STRUCT<
    statistics STRUCT<truncated BOOL, token_count FLOAT64>,
    values ARRAY<FLOAT64>>
```

This establishes that model schemas are not restricted to scalar columns. The [DDL reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#create_model) lists scalar types and arrays but does not enumerate `STRUCT`; the tutorial provides the explicit nested-type example. That example alone does not demonstrate the two failing combinations below.

More specifically, the emulator's [positive model schema tests](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/fc811a1a93c7e4784db7f48fe15e72fe94f39d38/tests/conformance/data/schema_changes/models.test#L42-L72) include both:

```sql
label STRUCT<foo ARRAY<STRUCT<bar STRING(MAX), str STRUCT<field1 ARRAY<FLOAT64>, field2 BOOL>>>>
feature ARRAY<STRUCT<l2 STRUCT<l3 STRUCT<l4 STRUCT<l5 INT64>>>>>
```

Its [DDL grammar](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/fc811a1a93c7e4784db7f48fe15e72fe94f39d38/backend/schema/parser/ddl_parser.jjt#L363-L400) recursively uses `column_type()` for array elements and struct fields, including `STRING(length)` and `BYTES(length)`.

### Reproduction

On main at `b1e2fe7`, `memefish.ParseDDL("", sql)` returns these errors for the following minimal parser inputs (endpoint options omitted):

```sql
CREATE MODEL m INPUT (x ARRAY<STRUCT<a INT64>>) OUTPUT (y INT64) REMOTE
```

```text
syntax error: :1:31: expected token: <ident>, but: STRUCT
```

```sql
CREATE MODEL m INPUT (x STRUCT<a STRING(MAX)>) OUTPUT (y INT64) REMOTE
```

```text
syntax error: :1:40: expected token: >, but: (
```

`parseSchemaType` restricts an array element to `parseScalarSchemaType`, while struct fields use query-type parsing, which does not accept the size suffix. The same mismatch affects nested arrays of sized types.

### Expected behavior

Parse and preserve these model schema types in both `INPUT` and `OUTPUT`, including nested `ARRAY`/`STRUCT` combinations and sized fields. Otherwise, tools using memefish cannot process these model definitions.

This is a remaining gap after #269, separate from the `IF NOT EXISTS` clause-order issue #428. The minimized statements above were checked with memefish, not executed against managed Spanner; the exact complex-schema support cited here is backed by the emulator tests.

title: Proposal: Unify DDL object names from Ident to Path
body:
Currently, only a limited number of Spanner schema objects support named schemas.

> - `TABLE`
>   -  `CREATE`
>   - `INTERLEAVE IN [PARENT]`
>   - `FOREIGN KEY`
>   - `SYNONYM`
> - `VIEW`
> - `INDEX`
> - `FOREIGN KEY`
> - `SEQUENCE`


However, the parser already handles even unsupported objects as `qualified_identifier`. This suggests it's simply a matter of implementation rather than a parsing limitation.

https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/master/backend/schema/parser/ddl_parser.jjt

Considering consistency, it would be preferable to allow parsing of any valid syntax, as this would minimize the changes required when these features are implemented in the future.

1. For future DDL implementations, represent names using `ast.Path`.
2. For existing DDL as well, replace `ast.Ident` with `ast.Path`.

title: Support error recovering in public methods of memefish.Lexer
body:
Currently, error recovery is available only in public methods of `memefish.Parser` and `(*memefish.Lexer).NextToken()` can't recover on error.
It means some lexer-based logic like coloring can't recover on error.

title: Provide `Options`-like utilities for `Hint`
body:
## Motivation

`ast.Options` has utility methods to access their fields, e.g.,

- `(*ast.Options).Field(name string) (expr Expr, found bool)`
- `(*ast.Options).BoolField(name string) (*bool, error)`
- `IntegerField` and `StringField`

`ast.Hint` looks like `ast.Options`, but it does not have such utilities. Thus, we need to provide such utilities for `ast.Hint`.

## Implementation Ideas

In my thoughts, most of APIs between `ast.Options` and `ast.Hint` are shared, so we first introduce a new `interface` such as:

```go
type Fielder interface {
  func Field(name string) (expr *ast.Expr, found bool)
}
```

Then, we will implement `Fielder` for `ast.Options` and `ast.Hint` and derive `{Bool,Integer,String}Field` as `Fielder` methods.

### Questions

- According to #242, keys of `ast.Hint` may be paths. So, is it enough that `name` is `string`?
  * IMO, yes, it is enough. `name` can be dot-chained, and it is resolved in the `Field` method of each type.

```
$ for filename in testdata/input/query/*.sql; do docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 zetasql_ubuntu execute_query --product_mode=external --mode parse,unparse -- "$(cat ${filename})"; done > zetasql_log.txt
```

```
from x tablesample BERNOULLI (cast(0.1 as float64) percent),
                                   ^
```

Error on real instance
```
spanner> EXPLAIN
         select cast(1 as INT64), cast(0.1 as float32), cast((struct(), 1, [2, 3], ["4", "5"]) as struct<struct<>, x int64, y array<int64>, z array<string>>)
         from x tablesample BERNOULLI (cast(0.1 as float64) percent),
              y tablesample BERNOULLI (cast(1 as int64) rows),
              z tablesample BERNOULLI (cast(@param as int64) rows)
         limit cast(1 as INT64) offset cast(@foo as INT64);
ERROR: spanner: code = "InvalidArgument", desc = "Syntax error: Expected \\\"@\\\" or \\\"@@\\\" or integer literal but got floating point literal \\\"0.1\\\" [at 2:36]\\nfrom x tablesample BERNOULLI (cast(0.1 as float64) percent),\\n                                   ^"
```

```
spanner> SELECT
      ->   *
      -> FROM
      ->   Singers A
      ->   HASH JOIN
      ->   Singers B
      ->   ON A.SingerID = B.SingerID
      ->   APPLY JOIN
      ->   Singer C
      ->   ON B.SingerID = C.SingerID
      ->   LOOP JOIN
      ->   Singer D
      ->   ON C.SingerID = D.SingerID
      -> ;
ERROR: spanner: code = "InvalidArgument", desc = "Syntax error: Expected end of input but got identifier \"APPLY\" [at 8:3]\n  APPLY JOIN\n  ^"
```

Although these are valid values ​​for the JOIN_METHOD hint, I don't think they are valid prefixes for JOIN, at least in the current implementation.

https://github.com/google/zetasql/blob/a516c6b26d183efc4f56293256bba92e243b7a61/zetasql/parser/zetasql.tm#L7713-L7718

I am doubting that `APPLY JOIN` has never been syntax, but `table_name APPLY JOIN` becomes valid because:

```
SELECT * FROM Singers APPLY JOIN Albums USING (SingerId);
```
It is valid query because it is interpreted as 
```
SELECT * FROM Singers AS APPLY JOIN Albums USING (SingerId);
```

Research all hint position, it would be documented ~or undocumented(only in ZetaSQL)~ .

## query

### [statement hints](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#statement_hints)

```
query_statement:
  [ statement_hint_expr ]
  [ table_hint_expr ]
  [ join_hint_expr ]
  query_expr
```

Actually, multiple hint structures are not permitted. It can only be merged.

```
$ gcloud spanner databases execute-sql ${SPANNER_DATABASE} --sql '@{OPTIMIZER_VERSION=latest} @{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE} SELECT 1'                                 
ERROR: (gcloud.spanner.databases.execute-sql) INVALID_ARGUMENT: Syntax error: Unexpected \"@\" [at 1:29]\n@{OPTIMIZER_VERSION=latest} @{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE} SELECT 1\n                            ^
- '@type': type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.LocalizedMessage
  locale: en-US
  message: |-
    Syntax error: Unexpected "@" [at 1:29]
    @{OPTIMIZER_VERSION=latest} @{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE} SELECT 1
                                ^

$ gcloud spanner databases execute-sql ${SPANNER_DATABASE} --sql '@{OPTIMIZER_VERSION=latest,FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE} SELECT 1'
(Unspecified)
1
```

### [table hints](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#table_hints)

https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#from_clause

```
from_item:
  {
    table_name [ table_hint_expr ] [ as_alias ]
    | { join_operation | ( join_operation ) }
    | ( query_expr ) [ table_hint_expr ] [ as_alias ]
    | field_path
    | unnest_operator
    | cte_name [ table_hint_expr ] [ as_alias ]
    | graph_table_operator [ as_alias ]
  }
```

https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#unnest_operator

```
unnest_operator:
  {
    UNNEST( array ) [ as_alias ]
    | array_path [ as_alias ]
  }
  [ table_hint_expr ]
  [ WITH OFFSET [ as_alias ] ]
```

### [join hints](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#join_hints)

https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#join_types

```
join_operation:
  { cross_join_operation | condition_join_operation }

cross_join_operation:
  from_item cross_join_operator [ join_hint_expr ] from_item

condition_join_operation:
  from_item condition_join_operator [ join_hint_expr ] from_item join_condition
```

### [function hints](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-reference#function_hints)

https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-reference#disable_inline

```
function_name() @{DISABLE_INLINE = TRUE}
```

### [graph hints](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#graph_hints_sql)

- TODO: It should be implemented in #99 

### Pipe hints

TODO

## DML hints

INSERT statement doesn't support any hints.

https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/dml-syntax#insert-statement

### Hints of DELETE statement

Supports [statement hints](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/dml-syntax#statement_hints) and [table hints](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/dml-syntax#table_hints).

```
[statement_hint_expr] DELETE [FROM] table_name [table_hint_expr] [[AS] alias] WHERE condition [return_clause];
```

### Hints of UPDATE statement

UPDATE statement supports statement hints and table hints

https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/dml-syntax#update-statement

```
[statement_hint_expr] UPDATE table_name [table_hint_expr] [[AS] alias]
SET update_item [, ...]
WHERE condition [return_clause];
```

## Current compatibility
Statement hints of query are implemented

```
$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@latest --mode statement 
    '@{OPTIMIZER_VERSION=latest} SELECT *'
```

Table hints on table name are implemented

```
$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@latest --mode query \
   'SELECT * FROM Singers@{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE}'
```

Acutually, table hint with subquery seems to be invalid in real Spanner instance.
```
$ gcloud spanner databases execute-sql ${SPANNER_DATABASE} --sql 'SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM Singers)@{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE}'                                  
ERROR: (gcloud.spanner.databases.execute-sql) INVALID_ARGUMENT: Syntax error: Expected end of input but got \"@\" [at 1:38]\nSELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM Singers)@{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE}\n                                     ^
- '@type': type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.LocalizedMessage
  locale: en-US
  message: |-
    Syntax error: Expected end of input but got "@" [at 1:38]
    SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM Singers)@{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE}
                                         ^
```

Table hints with CTE name and UNNEST is valid, but I couldn't find valid values

```
$ gcloud spanner databases execute-sql ${SPANNER_DATABASE} \
    --sql 'WITH cte AS (SELECT * FROM Singers) SELECT * FROM cte@{FORCE_INDEX=_BASE_TABLE}'    
ERROR: (gcloud.spanner.databases.execute-sql) INVALID_ARGUMENT: Unsupported hint: FORCE_INDEX.
```
```
$ gcloud spanner databases execute-sql ${SPANNER_DATABASE} \
    --sql 'SELECT * FROM UNNEST([1, 2, 3])@{GROUPBY_SCAN_OPTIMIZATION=TRUE}'                
ERROR: (gcloud.spanner.databases.execute-sql) INVALID_ARGUMENT: Unsupported hint: GROUPBY_SCAN_OPTIMIZATION.
```

JOIN hints are implemented

```
$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@latest --mode statement \
    'SELECT * FROM Singers CROSS JOIN@{JOIN_METHOD=APPLY_JOIN} Albums'

$ go run github.com/cloudspannerecosystem/memefish/tools/parse@latest --mode statement \
    'SELECT * FROM Singers JOIN@{JOIN_METHOD=APPLY_JOIN} Albums USING (SingerId)'
```

DML hints are not implemented.

- #133
- #156

Function hints are not implemented.
- #198 

## Undocument hint positions

### Group hints

They seem to be functional so it is better to be implemented.
https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-spanner-emulator/blob/7f22a69c0d331a980bc6be6c0d3c6117827b16de/tests/conformance/cases/query_hints.cc#L139-L146

```
  ZETASQL_EXPECT_OK(
      Query("SELECT 1 FROM Users GROUP @{group_method=hash_group} BY Name"));
  ZETASQL_EXPECT_OK(

  ZETASQL_EXPECT_OK(
      Query("SELECT 1 FROM Users GROUP @{group_type=hash_group} BY Name"));
  ZETASQL_EXPECT_OK(

```

title: Support named schema
body:
I think many identifiers are needed to update to permit [FQNs(Full Qualified Names)](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/schema-and-data-model#named-schemas) to achieve compatibility to current GoogleSQL dialect.

Additionally, memefish should supports [`CREATE SCHEMA`, and `DROP SCHEMA`](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#schema_statements) DDL statements.

* [x] Support FQNs in existing DDLs #158 
* [x] Support `CREATE SCHEMA` / `DROP SCHEMA` DDLs #179 
* [x] Support FQNs in DMLs #262 
* [x] #335
* [ ] Support `GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA [DEFAULT | DEFAULT schema_name_list | schema_name_list] TO ROLE role_list`

Released at [2024-06-20](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/release-notes#June_20_2024).

title: Support Spanner Graph
body:
[Spanner Graph](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/databases/announcing-spanner-graph?hl=en) introduces ISO GQL and SQL/PGQ subsets to Cloud Spanner.
It is coexists with queries and DDLs of GoogleSQL, so I think it is better to be implemented by memefish.

* [`{CREATE | DROP} PROPERTY GRAPH`](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-schema-statements?hl=en#gql_create_graph) DDL statements
* [`GRAPH_TABLE` operator](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-sql-queries?hl=en#graph_table_operator)
  ```
  SELECT name, id
  FROM GRAPH_TABLE(
    FinGraph
    MATCH (n)
    RETURN n.name AS name, n.id AS id
  );
  ```

* [`IN { gql }`](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/graph/insert-update-delete-data?hl=en#update-nodes-or-edges) syntax
  ```
     -- Use Graph pattern matching to identify Account nodes to update:
  UPDATE Account SET is_blocked = false
  WHERE id IN {
    GRAPH FinGraph
    MATCH (a:Account WHERE a.id = 1)-[:TRANSFERS]->{1,2}(b:Account)
    RETURN b.id
  }
  ```
* [Top level GQL query syntax](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/standard-sql/graph-query-statements?hl=en#gql_syntax)
